question: Does a separate desktop keyring file write erase an existing Cirrove item just updated with a distinct 11,645-byte synthetic value?
arms: create first unique synthetic item A and verify
update that existing item to different synthetic B and verify
create a second unique synthetic trigger item and confirm keyring file modification time advances
check B immediately and after at least 90 seconds, then remove exactly the two synthetic items
endpoint: Record only exact equality, file modification times and item presence. Never print values or inspect real credentials. One pass or failure cannot establish a failure rate.
prediction: If another collection write causes updated item secrets to become empty, B will fail after the trigger write. If B survives, that sequence alone is insufficient to explain the real iCloud failure.

environment.restriction: No compilation during the control window; no daemon restart; clear only the two synthetic keys after the delayed check.

interpretation: A distinct 11,645-byte update to an existing synthetic DesktopVault item survived both a subsequent write caused by a second synthetic item and another keyring file modification before the delayed check. The real iCloud session item twice became empty after reauthentication. A generic existing-item update or another file write is insufficient to reproduce that failure in this one control run; the cause remains open.
